newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eramet rejects criticism on N.Caledonia.
newsitem.headline: Eramet rejects criticism on N.Caledonia.

text.p: French nickel group Eramet rejected on Tuesday criticism made by state holding Erap against the way Eramet managers had handled a dispute over the distribution of mining assets in New Caledonia.

In a letter to Erap's president Remy Chardon, disclosed by French daily la Tribune and later obtained by Reuters, the nine members of the management committee of Eramet said the criticism was "unfounded" and the method used by Chardon "particularly shocking".
The letter was signed by the nine top officials representing Eramet and its units Societe Le Nickel and Erasteel.
The committee said it had taken the unusual step to make the letter public and voice its "indignation" in light of the "extreme seriousness" of the criticism made.

Chardon, who became a board member of Eramet on April 16, had told French daily La Tribune last week that he blamed Eramet's managers for having wasted "an enormous amount of time" in the New Caledonia mining row.
The French state and Eramet have been involved in a dispute over a controversial plan to build a new nickel smelter in the north of the French teritory.
The government wants to use some of Eramet's mining reserves to supply a future plant of Canadian group Falconbridge and the local Kanak company Societe Miniere de Sud Pacifique (SMSP).
Eramet has repeatedly said it did not oppose the plan as long as it did not threaten its own development in New Caledonia.

Erap also plans to seek control of Eramet's board at the next shareholders' meeting on May 28. If approved the motion may pave the way for the ouster of Chairman Yves Rambaud, industry sources have said.

In the letter the committee said Chardon was making Eramet's managers responsible for delays that stemmed from the "chaotic handling of the affair" while Eramet had been "intentionally locked out" of the talks during several months.
It also critised Chardon for having publicly attacked Eramet's managers on the eve of crucial talks with Falconbridge and SMSP and reiterated its support for Rambaud.

"We deeply regret to have been forced to make our reaction public. Our intention was never to feed the dispute, the main issue being, in total solidarity with Yves Rambaud, to seek an industrial and fair solution that would balance the general interest and the interest of Eramet," the letter said.
The heads of Eramet, SMSP, Falconbridge and Erap met last Friday in Paris to discuss the plans to build a new smelter.
In a joint statement issued after the meeting they said they had found common ground for the project and that experts would be brought in to study the problems identified during the meeting.
Chardon told Reuters on Monday that the talks had been "very positive" and that he hoped to get an agreement soon.
